<issue>
Directory deletion not cascading to child file records in index
## Summary

When a **subdirectory containing source files** is deleted from the project, CodeGraph fails to detect the change and does not update the SQLite index. The deleted files remain in the database, and index counts (files, nodes, edges) stay unchanged.

This appears to be a **cascade deletion bug**: removing a parent directory does not trigger removal of its child file records from the index.

## Reproduction Steps

1. `codegraph init` — initialize index
2. Create nested source file: `docs/1/2/新建文件夹/_0204_.py`
3. Wait for CodeGraph to sync (check `Last Sync` timestamp)
4. **Delete the subdirectory `docs/1`** (which contains `_0204_.py`)
5. Observe: index counts unchanged, deleted file still appears in queries

## Attachment: Diagnostic Tool

I built a lightweight real-time monitor (`codegraph_state.js`) to visualize this bug. It displays live index counts alongside filesystem events, making the mismatch immediately obvious.

**Author: feel free to use or adapt this tool for debugging.**

[codegraph_state.js](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30005409/codegraph_state.js)

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed, find the file watcher / sync code that handles file deletion (directory delete events, e.g. chokidar/fs.watch, 'unlink', removeFile, getChangedFiles in sync/extraction). Report relevant file paths and code snippets with line numbers, how deleted files are detected (watcher events and sync diff against DB).

content.content: {"summary":"Deletions are detected in two layers. The watcher (src/sync/watcher.ts) only marks a changed path as pending and schedules a sync; it never removes rows. The real deletion happens in sync() (src/extraction/index.ts), which diffs the filesystem against the DB by path and deletes tracked rows whose file is gone. getChangedFiles() is read-only and reports the same removals, using git status in git projects and a full scan otherwise.","findings":["src/sync/watcher.ts:416-419: on macOS/Windows one recursive fs.watch(root, {recursive:true}) feeds all events, including deletes, into handleChange(normalizePath(String(filename))). The event type is not checked.","src/sync/watcher.ts:~520-537 (handleDirEvent): on Linux each directory has its own fs.watch. If fs.statSync(full) throws (path vanished, i.e. deleted), the event falls through to handleChange as a normal change.","src/sync/watcher.ts:550-572 (handleChange): applies isAlwaysIgnored, ignoreMatcher and isSourceFile filters, records the path in pendingFiles (~line 559), then calls scheduleSync(). Deletes and edits take the same path.","src/sync/watcher.ts:~760-800 (flush): runs syncFn, then removes pendingFiles entries with lastSeenMs <= syncStartedMs. On failure pendingFiles is kept for retry.","src/extraction/index.ts:2449-2510 (sync): currentFiles = scanDirectoryAsync(rootDir); trackedFiles = queries.getAllFiles(). Removal check at ~2490: `!currentSet.has(path) || !fs.existsSync(...)`. The existsSync check is needed because git ls-files still lists files deleted from disk but not staged. Incoming cross-file edges are resurrected as unresolved refs first (#1240). Then queries.deleteFile at ~2507 and filesRemoved++.","src/db/queries.ts:1876-1882: deleteFile runs 'DELETE FROM files WHERE path = ?'. Foreign-key cascade removes the file's nodes and edges.","src/extraction/index.ts:2605-2646 (getChangedFiles, git path): gitChanges.deleted (status code containing 'D') is reported as removed only if getFileByPath finds a tracked row. Added/modified files are hashed and compared to DB contentHash.","src/extraction/index.ts:2657-2691 (getChangedFiles fallback for non-git projects): full scanDirectory; any tracked path missing from the current set goes to removed (~2663-2667).","src/extraction/index.ts:~1124-1130 (collectGitStatus): deletions skip the ignore filter and go to out.deleted, so stale rows under newly excluded dirs get cleaned up (#766).","src/index.ts:1033-1034 exposes CodeGraph.getChangedFiles() by delegating to the orchestrator; src/bin/codegraph.ts:940 uses it for status output.","src/sync/watcher.ts:117-125: injectable watchImpl (default fs.watch) for tests. No chokidar is used in this codebase, despite some comments mentioning it. Line numbers marked ~ are approximate."],"confidence":0.75}

The failure is deterministic and reproduces when run alone.","findings":["tsc --noEmit -p . exited 0 with no output.","Failing test: __tests__/watcher.test.ts > FileWatcher > filtering > 'should ignore files not matching include patterns' (assertion at watcher.test.ts:447). expect(syncFn).not.toHaveBeenCalled() failed: the spy was called once with an empty array ([]), so a sync fired for a file that should be excluded by include patterns.","The failure reproduces when this test is run in isolation (vitest -t filter), so it is not caused by cross-test interference.","Other watcher-related files passed, including watch-policy, mcp-staleness-banner and mcp-catchup-gate. Their stderr noise (e.g. 'too many open files' from the staleness-banner test) is expected output from tests that simulate watcher failure, not failures."],"confidence":0.85}
